key_insight: The paper shows that nonnegativity adds a new identifiability signal—positive scattering—that can certify uniqueness of tensor decompositions beyond classical dimension-based criteria.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper test for when sparse nonnegative tensor factorizations are provably recoverable, which is useful for applications in signal processing, chemometrics, and latent-variable modeling.
method: Add a positive scattering term to the Lovitz–Petrov/Kruskal-style dimension budget.
Use subset-wise thresholds: $2|S|-2$ for minimality/nonnegative rank and $2|S|-1$ for uniqueness among same-length nonnegative decompositions.
Derive a positive splitting inequality for irreducible exchanges and characterize activation via graph connectivity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the criterion can certify sparse nonnegative tensor decompositions even in cases where Kruskal and Lovitz–Petrov conditions fail, including after reshaping, and it reduces to known matrix factorizations in the matrix case.
watch_item: The scattering term is defined through an optimization over intermediate factor spaces, so practical use may require careful computation and may be expensive for large tensors.
paper_title: Identifiability of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions via Positive Scattering
